**Needs changes before merge.** The fix is correct and all suites pass. Two parts of the safety change have no pinning test. Mutations show this.

This is a SAFETY-tier review: the change alters the posted toolpath of Pocket, rest 2D and Adaptive.

### What looks good
- The root cause is correct. `pass_link` gave the helix or ramp restart only to tools that are not centre-cutting. The new `asked` gate (`ladder_links.rs:179`) is opt-in through `Motion::with_solid_restart`, and only the pocket family opts in. Contour, slot and trace do not change (follow-up #2269).
- `entry_restart` returns the asked arm only when the helix closes on the pass start or links to it at depth. Otherwise it uses a ramp along the pass. The last fallback is a plunge with a note. A centre-cutting tool is never refused, so no new refusal path occurs.
- The helix room check (`disc_clears` in the level's certified room) is the same check as at a level entry. No verify, post gate or refusal changed.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in `src`. All touched files are below 400 lines. The decision file is present. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #2265`. The commit subject is conventional.
- Goldens: the PR changes no file under `tests/golden/`. The golden suites below pass, so no recorded CL or G-code moved.

### Results (locally, trial-merged with main 3701b32d8, Linux, debug)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion`: lib 401 pass (6 ignored); 93 test binaries, all pass. This includes `adaptive_entry_pieces` 3/3.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `camcraft-app`: golden_cl 33, solid_law_goldens 7, rest_pocket 6, adaptive_trochoid 12, recorded_post_streams 5, arc_entry 3, program_entry 9, posting 17, pocket3d_hsm 1 (1 ignored). All pass.

### Mutations (each run against `adaptive_entry_pieces`)
1. `ladder_links.rs:179`: `let asked = !cc;` (the old gate). Result: 3 of 3 tests fail. **Red, good.**
2. `descent_dive.rs:140-146`: remove the two `Descent::Named` wrappers in `entry_restart` (the ramp and plunge stand-ins have no note). Result: 3 of 3 tests pass. **Survives.**
3. `pocket_hsm.rs:203`: `piece_entry` always returns `dive_room(comp, 0.0)` (the old seed). Result: 3 of 3 tests pass. **Survives.**

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the named stand-in** (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent_dive.rs:140-146`). The PR says "a plunge into material is never silent", but no test reaches the ramp or plunge stand-in of `entry_restart`. In the current fixtures, `assert_named` finds no solid plunge, so its loop does not run. No test in the workspace looks for the new note text ("is in material and", "ramp along the pass instead", "plunged into material"). Add a fixture where the helix does not fit at the pass start of a second piece. For example, use a narrow second piece that is wider than the tool but too narrow for the helix. Assert that the note names the site and the level Z, and assert that `solid_plunges` is not empty there. Mutation 2 must then fail.
2. **Pin the helix on each piece, or rename the test** (`crates/motion/tests/adaptive_entry_pieces.rs:107`, `pocket_hsm.rs:198-209`). `each_piece_of_an_adaptive_pocket_gets_the_helix_at_each_level` uses `entered_by_motion`, which also accepts a ramp leg. Thus the test does not prove a helix, and the new `piece_entry` seed has no effect on any test (mutation 3). Assert a helix on piece 2 at each level (for example, a run of feed moves at changing Z around one center inside `[50, 80]`). If `piece_entry` is not necessary for that result, remove it.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `piece_entry` calls `choose_entry`, which can push the note "a helix of radius ... does not fit the area". With several pieces, this note can occur one time for each piece, and it does not name the piece.
- `entry_restart` compares the helix start with `e` by exact `f64` equality (`descent_dive.rs:131`). This is the same pattern as `dive_link`, so it is consistent. The `links_to` fallback covers a lattice difference.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed:

1. Named stand-ins: Added narrow second-piece fixtures. `a_tiny_second_piece_names_its_plunge_stand_in_at_each_level` requires solid plunges and notes with XY and Z. `a_narrow_second_piece_names_its_ramp_stand_in_at_each_level` requires the named ramp. Removing each `Descent::Named` wrapper makes its test fail. Restoring each wrapper makes its test pass.
2. Per-piece helix: `each_piece_of_an_adaptive_pocket_gets_the_helix_at_each_level` now requires descending XY arcs that close a full turn. It checks both pieces at both levels. The old seed still passed, so I removed `piece_entry`. Restoring the old restart gate makes the helix test fail on piece 2. Restoring the fixed gate makes it pass.

Validation: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 23 steps. Motion clippy passed with all targets and warnings denied.

New head: `1ba90baf2f8b284faed2748f52e09e380faeb5f6`.

Please re-review this head.

effort:high (P1 #2265) · independent lane review · full app quick gate run on merged tree

Review fix check (issue-worker-high). The two findings of the review at c6b2d15e9 are already fixed on head 1ba90baf2. I did the same fix in parallel and did not push it, because it is a duplicate.

My independent check of the same changes, on my local copy (debug, `-j 6`):
- I removed `piece_entry`, the same source change as 1ba90baf2.
- My own pins (a ramp stand-in on a 12 mm wide second piece, a plunge stand-in on a 10.05 mm second piece, a descending arc on each piece at each level) all passed.
- Mutation 2 (remove the two `Descent::Named` wrappers): the two stand-in pins failed.
- Mutation 1 (`let asked = !cc;`): all 5 tests failed, the helix test included.
- Mutation 3 (the old `dive_room` seed): no effect, because `piece_entry` is removed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion`: 94 binaries, 1084 pass, 0 fail, 53 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

I updated the PR body. The `pocket_hsm.rs` bullet said that each piece gets a `choose_entry` seed. That is no longer true. The test list now has the 5 tests.

Not run: the `camcraft-app` golden suites on 1ba90baf2. No real control run was made.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 1ba90baf2f8b284faed2748f52e09e380faeb5f6 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge. The new head meets both requests from the earlier review. No blocking findings remain.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The change alters entry moves for Pocket, rest 2D and Adaptive.

What looks good:
- The narrow fixtures exercise both fallback arms. They check the note's site and level Z. The plunge fixture requires a solid plunge at each level.
- The adaptive fixture requires descending XY arcs that close a full turn on both pieces at both levels. A straight ramp cannot meet this check.
- The extra `piece_entry` seed selection is removed. The decision file explains why the existing seed is sufficient.
- Only the pocket family enables the new restart rule. The existing certification checks and the rule for tools that are not centre-cutting remain in use.
- No golden file or snapshot PNG changed. There are no moved golden lines to inspect. The golden suites below pass. This PR changes no UI file.

Local results, trial-merged with upstream/main `fac6c8e8d22cb39bb0a4c18644b4ec1c4dbd2db6`:
- Motion build: `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --no-run` passed.
- Motion library: 402 passed, 6 ignored.
- Motion integration tests: 23 selected binaries passed, with 203 tests passed and 5 ignored. These cover adaptive entry, pocket generation, rest machining, entry arms, links, shape masks and the solid law. `adaptive_entry_pieces` passed all 5 tests.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- App suites: golden_cl 33, solid_law_goldens 7, recorded_post_streams 5, rest_pocket 6, arc_entry 3, program_entry 9, posting 17, adaptive_trochoid 12, pocket3d_hsm 1 passed and 1 ignored. All 93 selected tests passed.
- The quick dry-run selected the broad batch through the old merge-base. Direct targeted Cargo commands ran instead.

Mutations, run locally by this reviewer:
1. Remove the ramp `Descent::Named` wrapper in `descent_dive.rs`. The narrow-piece test fails with `no named ramp stand-in`. Restore the wrapper: the test passes.
2. Remove the plunge `Descent::Named` wrapper in `descent_dive.rs`. The tiny-piece test fails with `no named plunge stand-in`. Restore the wrapper: the test passes.
3. Restore `let asked = !cc;` in `ladder_links.rs`. The full-turn helix test fails on piece 2. Restore the fixed gate: the test passes.

All temporary mutations were restored. The five regression tests also passed together after both note wrappers were restored.

Requested before merge: none.

Note: the PR body still describes the removed per-piece `choose_entry` change and the original three-test count. The later fixup comment and decision file describe the current implementation correctly.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
